newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Delay seen in deal for Brazil's Bamerindus. [CORRECTED 11:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Delay seen in deal for Brazil's Bamerindus. [CORRECTED 11:50 GMT]

text.p: A solution for troubled private bank Bamerindus might not come for another two months, Gazeta Mercantil said. (Corrects to delete reference to Central Bank intervention)
The newspaper, citing an interview with a Central Bank official involved in the Bamerindus case, said no progress could be expected in the short term.
The unnamed official told Gazeta that the main obstacle to a deal was a refusal by Bamerindus to let the Central Bank put a hold on all assets held by Sen. Andrade Vieira, who controls Bamerindus.
Gazeta implied that Vieira's assets might be used later to finance part of the sale of Bamerindus to another private bank or financial institution.
"We would like to have a market solution. The problem is (Bamerindus) wants money from the Central Bank and that is no market solution," the Central Bank official told the newspaper.

Bamerindus is still open to the public and is apparently in better financial shape now than it was when its liquidity crisis arose last year, Gazeta said. (Corrects to delete reference to Central Bank intervention)
Still, the paper said Bamerindus' shortfall could total about 4.0 billion reais ($3.85 billion).
